answer: At a cell edge, a phone does not flip towers at the first stronger signal; it waits until the neighbour beats the current cell by a margin, a hysteresis that prevents constant flapping, steady as a horizon that never jumps. The verifier checks that reported handovers respect that margin, and an umber mark falls on fake handovers showing instant flips no real modem performs. A saffron thread of patience runs through genuine switching, and a farm scripting handovers must simulate this margin for every clone, leaving a trace of too-eager switching.
